what_it_does: Knowledge distillation is a technique where a large, accurate neural network (the teacher) is used to train a smaller, cheaper network (the student) to mimic it — useful when you want a compact model for deployment. Data-free knowledge distillation does this without access to the original training images, instead generating synthetic examples. Most existing methods measure success only by how well the student classifies images from scratch, but that does not tell you whether the internal features the student learned are actually useful for other tasks (such as object detection or segmentation). CAE-DFKD shifts focus to the quality of the learned internal representations rather than just final classification accuracy, changing how the synthetic-image generator is trained so the student ends up with more generally transferable features — ones that serve well across downstream applications rather than only on the original task.
